records.literal_gloss: Praise YHWH, all nations; extol him, all the peoples.

en.L: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all nations; extol {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, all the peoples!
en.B: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, every nation! Sing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praises, all you peoples!
en.R: All you nations, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! People everywhere, give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} honor!

fr.L: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, toutes les nations ; célébrez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, tous les peuples !
fr.B: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, vous, toutes les nations ! Chantez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} louange, vous, tous les peuples !
fr.R: Vous, toutes les nations, louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Gens du monde entier, rendez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} honneur !

sw.L: Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, enyi mataifa yote; msifuni kwa sauti, enyi watu wote!
sw.B: Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kila taifa! Imbeni sifa {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, enyi watu wote!
sw.R: Enyi mataifa yote, msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Watu wa kila mahali, mpeni heshima!

decisions.reason: Psalm 117 has only two verses, the shortest chapter in the Bible. It calls every nation to praise the God of Israel.
Paul quotes this verse to show that the nations were always meant to praise God for his mercy (Romans 15:8-11).
The verb (shibbach) is to praise loudly, to commend (63:4; 145:4).

source.text: כִּ֥י גָ֘בַ֤ר עָלֵ֨ינוּ׀חַסְדּ֗וֹ וֶֽאֱמֶת־יְהוָ֥ה לְעוֹלָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For mighty over us [is] his loyal love, and [the] faithfulness of YHWH [is] forever. Praise Yah!

en.L: For mighty over us [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and the faithfulness of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] forever. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love toward us is overwhelming, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stays faithful forever. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.R: His faithful love for us is very great, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will always be faithful. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

fr.L: Car puissant sur nous [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour loyal, et la fidélité {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [est] pour toujours. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour fidèle envers nous est immense, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} reste fidèle pour toujours. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !
fr.R: Son amour fidèle pour nous est très grand, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sera toujours fidèle. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !

sw.L: Kwa maana upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma [ni] mkuu juu yetu, na uaminifu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] wa milele. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}!
sw.B: Kwa maana upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwetu ni mwingi mno, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anadumu mwaminifu milele. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}!
sw.R: Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwetu ni mkuu sana, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuwa mwaminifu daima. Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}!

decisions.reason: The verb (gavar) is to be strong, to prevail. His love has proved stronger than anything against his people (103:11).
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
The nations are called to praise for the love shown to "us", God's people. Paul saw in it the joining of the nations with Israel (Romans 15:10-11).

The Hebrew is two words: a plural command, "praise!" (hallelu), and Yah, the short form of the divine name (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It calls the gathered people to praise. Like the full name, Yah is rendered "the LORD", with Yah as the alternative.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
